source_text: V. Post hanc vero sententiam turba fratrum dicebat: Et nos cum ipso decollemur. propter hoc tumultus fratrum exortus est et multa turba eum prosecuta est. et ita idem Cyprianus in agrum Sexti productus est et ibi se lacerna byrro exspoliavit et genu in terra flexit et in orationem se domino prostravit. et cum se dalmatica exspoliasset et diaconibus tradidisset, in linea stetit et coepit spiculatorem sustinere. cum venisset autem spiculator, iussit suis ut eidem spiculatori viginti quinque aureos darent. linteamina vero et manualia a fratribus ante eum mittebantur. postea vero beatus Cyprianus manu sua oculos sibi texit. qui cum lacinias manuales ligare sibi non potuisset, Iulianus presbyter et Iulianus subdiaconus ei ligaverunt. ita beatus Cyprianus passus est, eiusque corpus propter gentilium curiositatem in proximo positum est. inde per noctem sublatum cum cereis et scolacibus ad areas Macrobii Candidiani procuratoris, quae sunt in via Mappaliensi, iuxta piscinas, cum voto et triumpho magno deductum est. post paucos autem dies Galerius Maximus proconsul decessit.
thought_title: Beheaded at the field and carried away by night
orientation: After Cyprian thanks God for the death sentence, the crowd of fellow Christians follows him to the execution ground where he is beheaded and his body is later removed for burial.
pass_a_gloss: But after this sentence the crowd of fellow Christians was saying: Let us also be beheaded with him. On account of this an uproar of the fellow Christians arose and a great crowd followed him. And so the same Cyprian was led out into the field of Sextus and there he stripped himself of hooded cloak and outer cloak and bent his knee on the ground and threw himself down to the Lord in prayer. And when he had stripped himself of his dalmatic robe and had handed it over to the deacons, he stood in a linen tunic and began to await the executioner. But when the executioner had come, he ordered his own people to give to the same executioner twenty five gold pieces. But linen cloths and hand cloths were being laid before him by the fellow Christians. But afterwards blessed Cyprian covered his eyes for himself with his own hand. And since he was not able to tie the strips of the hand cloth for himself, Julian the priest and Julian the subdeacon tied them for him. Thus blessed Cyprian suffered, and his body was placed nearby on account of the curiosity of the pagans. From there taken up through the night with wax candles and torches it was conducted with vow and great triumph to the grounds of Macrobius Candidianus the procurator, which are on the Mappalian road, beside the fish ponds. But after a few days Galerius Maximus the governor died.

pass_b_english: After this sentence the crowd of fellow Christians said, "Let us be beheaded with him." An uproar among the fellow Christians broke out over this, and a large crowd followed him. So Cyprian was led out to the field of Sextus. There he stripped off his hooded cloak and thick outer cloak, bent his knee to the ground, and threw himself before the Lord in prayer. When he had stripped off his long tunic and handed it to the deacons, he stood in his linen tunic and began to await the executioner.

When the executioner arrived, Cyprian ordered his own people to give the executioner twenty-five gold pieces. Linen cloths and handkerchiefs were laid before him by fellow Christians. Then blessed Cyprian covered his eyes with his own hand. Since he could not tie the ends of the handkerchief for himself, Julian the priest and Julian the subdeacon tied them for him. So blessed Cyprian suffered, and his body was laid nearby because of the curiosity of the pagans. Then by night it was taken up and carried with candles and torches to the grounds of Macrobius Candidianus on the Mappalian Way near the pools, escorted with vows and great triumph. A few days later Galerius Maximus the governor died.
notes: scolacibus is obscure or corrupt; glossed from context as torches carried with wax candles in a night procession
